checks: Checked 9402605e47a1b4ef §1, equality paragraph. The t=0 exposed face of the auxiliary lifted body is exactly the original compact convex set. Its full-dimensional ball in the t=1 plane and any point at t=0 make the auxiliary hull full dimensional. The added variable is a base coordinate, so neither the d-volume nor the original continuous normals change on the face.

For each common normal, convexity and affinity put the weighted endpoint cap sum in the target cap. At an active target normal the chain has nonnegative gaps. Positive weights force both endpoint cap volumes to be active, classical Brunn–Minkowski equality gives positive homothety of full-dimensional caps, and equal-volume inclusion gives equality of the sets.

Conversely the specified cap gives the matching upper depth bound by homogeneity of the positively homothetic endpoint caps. Root concavity supplies the lower bound, so no independent condition on activity of the target cap is needed.

At positive own depth the endpoint mark is interior and every through-mark section is proper. Its active cap is stationary under all nonzero normals u+tw with threshold (u+tw)·x_i, not merely formally on a fixed sphere. The derivative forces its proper section centroid to be x_i. Positive homothety sends minimizing faces for the same u to each other. In dimension one those faces are singleton marks.

dependencies.hypotheses: Use joint concavity and ordinary cap attainment on the full-dimensional auxiliary body if needed. Taking the exposed face at auxiliary base zero recovers the exact fibers in R^d, with the same halfspace infimum.

Apply only §2 proper-trace variation, to the single full-dimensional positive endpoint fiber at a fixed base. Since x_i is interior, the zero-tangency condition is vacuous and the section has positive (d−1)-measure. The variation fixes the base normal and has (u',b')=(w,w·x_i). No projected-contact or ray-normal hypothesis is used.
